title: CISA 2026 learning outline
effective: August 2024 exam content outline (current in ISACA 2026 Candidate Guide, version 1.26)

topics.title: IS Audit Standards, Guidelines, Functions, and Codes of Ethics
topics.observation: the audit team accepted scope changes requested by the process owner without documenting independence safeguards
topics.risk: the assurance conclusion may be biased and fail to meet professional audit requirements
topics.control: document independence threats, obtain appropriate oversight, and align work with applicable standards
topics.evidence: the approved audit charter, independence declarations and approved engagement scope
topics.intro: This topic examines how an IS auditor evaluates is audit standards, guidelines, functions, and codes of ethics. The central concern is whether management has established appropriate ownership, expectations, evidence, and monitoring to keep technology risk within acceptable business limits.
topics.example: Consider an audit where the audit team accepted scope changes requested by the process owner without documenting independence safeguards. The underlying exposure is that the assurance conclusion may be biased and fail to meet professional audit requirements.
topics.auditApproach: Assess how the organization can document independence threats, obtain appropriate oversight, and align work with applicable standards. Seek persuasive evidence such as the approved audit charter, independence declarations and approved engagement scope and verify whether the control works in practice.

topics.auditApproach: Assess how the organization can distinguish advisory reviews from assurance engagements and communicate the level of assurance explicitly. Seek persuasive evidence such as the engagement terms, workpapers and final report distribution record and verify whether the control works in practice.

topics.risk: the same underlying defect may continue disrupting critical services
topics.control: connect incidents to root-cause analysis and controlled permanent fixes
topics.evidence: linked incident/problem records, root-cause analysis and validation results
topics.intro: This topic examines how an IS auditor evaluates problem and incident management. The central concern is whether management has established appropriate ownership, expectations, evidence, and monitoring to keep technology risk within acceptable business limits.
topics.example: Consider an audit where recurring incidents were closed as isolated tickets without problem analysis. The underlying exposure is that the same underlying defect may continue disrupting critical services.
topics.auditApproach: Assess how the organization can connect incidents to root-cause analysis and controlled permanent fixes. Seek persuasive evidence such as linked incident/problem records, root-cause analysis and validation results and verify whether the control works in practice.
